current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 111 of them on 5 October 2026: 39 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything (in our browser check of 3 Oct 2026, 3 of 6 demos ran on a machine without a GPU). Is it a brain or just a map? It is a map of one fly's wiring (a fly brain scan) run with a simple neuron model, and in our own pre-registered test of 5 Oct 2026 that wiring made a difference: We ran the map. A looming shadow on one eye turned our simulated fly away in 4 of 4 runs. With the same map scrambled (same number of connections per neuron) it turned away in 0 of 3. Here the map's wiring, not the stimulus or our code, makes the turn. One model (Shiu et al. LIF on FlyWire v783), open loop, our hand-made mapping, a constant external walking drive, 1 s; not a real fly. Caveats: only 4 real and 3 scrambled runs (pre-registered time limits; the scrambled runs sent identical drives); the scrambled brains were much quieter (activity ratio 0.50) and no activity-matched scramble was reached, so our ledger rates the comparison unfair and weak; the 'away' direction rests on our mapping's DNa02 sign and fly67's claim and was not verified in real flies. fly67's own brain rule was reproduced in our Brian2 run (giant fibre 111.5-120.5 Hz vs fly67's 114.8/120.3; far-side DNa02 23-44 Hz, near side 0), and fly67 stays grade B. Is it AI? The base model is not trained AI: it copies the wiring and sets one strength by hand; of 78 graded projects, 43 add a trained, learning or search-tuned part. Can it suffer? We found no study that measured consciousness or suffering in these models; fly larvae detect harmful heat and pressure, and whether flies feel pain is open. Can I put it in my game? Yes for a non-commercial project with credit, in our cautious reading of FlyWire's CC BY-NC 4.0 (not legal advice); MaleCNS is CC BY 4.0. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; no fly has been "uploaded". Gorilla Tag (868,853 views on 5 Oct 2026) still names no model, data or code and stays U; all 20 verdicts were re-checked (13 with code unchanged since graded, 7 with no code). Does the real fly wiring help? Sometimes: across 38 control studies it beat scrambled wiring in 13 of 30, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir, ML, game, robot-arm and our walking tests it tied or lost (10). Across 19 studies with a no-brain baseline the fly network beats it in only 3; in Doom a brainless autopilot survives 51.93 s against the fly brain's 53.34 s (doom-fly-control by gabrycina), and in our walking test a scrambled brain and no brain walked the FlyGym fly as far as the real brain. A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs sugar input drove MN9 to 85.2 Hz and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz; re-tested 5 Oct 2026 (6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz bit-exact), with tested deeper steps for a FlyGym body and a looming sense.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 111 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code: 39 you can try online, 53 videos with evidence grades and language labels, verdicts on 20 viral claims, 38 control studies, and our own tests: we ran the FlyWire map, and a looming shadow turned our simulated fly away in 4 of 4 runs with real wiring, 0 of 3 scrambled (small n, one model).

summary: 111 entries checked on 5 Oct 2026 (4 new in the eighth check): 25 grade A, 22 B, 27 C, 4 D, 9 U and 24 datasets or tools (not graded).

We ran the map (made by us, pre-registered at 09:42:47 UTC on 5 Oct 2026 before the first trial): We ran the map. A looming shadow on one eye turned our simulated fly away in 4 of 4 runs. With the same map scrambled (same number of connections per neuron) it turned away in 0 of 3. Here the map's wiring, not the stimulus or our code, makes the turn. One model (Shiu et al. LIF on FlyWire v783), open loop, our hand-made mapping, a constant external walking drive, 1 s; not a real fly. Real runs turned 34-68 degrees away (mean 51.6); left-eye shadows turned the fly right and right-eye shadows left (2 of 2 each); brainless random steering 'turned away' in 3 of 6; pre-registered reading 'the turn away needs the wiring' (scrambled retention 0.00; ledger single-floor method 0.0096).

Looming, brain: every LC4 and LPLC2 neuron of one eye (162 left, 152 right) at 80 Hz for 1 s in the Shiu et al. model on FlyWire v783 (Brian2 2.9.0). fly67's own pass rule reproduced in our Brian2 run: giant fibre 111.5-120.5 Hz (fly67's engine 114.8 / 120.3 Hz), far-side DNa02 23-44 Hz, near side 0 Hz. In all 3 degree-preserving shuffles the giant fibre and DNa02 stayed at 0 Hz and the brain fired about half as many spikes (activity ratio 0.50). fly67 stays grade B.

Plain answers with evidence on Is it real?: Is it AI? (the base model is not trained AI; 43 of 78 graded projects add trained, learning or tuned parts); Is it a brain or just a map? (a map run with a simple model; in our tests its wiring drove a reflex and a turn, body software did the walking); Can it suffer? (no study measured suffering in these models; whether flies feel pain is open); Can I put it in my game? (yes for non-commercial projects with credit, our cautious reading of CC BY-NC 4.0; not legal advice).

Controls ledger (5 Oct 2026): 38 studies, 30 with a wiring null: helps 13, no difference 8, worse 2, mixed 6, not yet scored 1. New: our looming test (helps; unfair null and weak method by the fixed rules), Flight-test the fly (helps, but a classical yaw damper does far better: 1.69 vs 3.19 deg/s), FlyAim (no difference: 412.5 vs 430.9 px, a random walker 251.7) and FlyArm (no difference by the ledger rules: 72.2% vs 55.9%, p = 0.125). No scoring rule changed.
Our walking test (2 Oct): real brain 13.93 mm, scrambled 14.15 mm, brainless constant drive 14.28 mm in 1 s; the legs are FlyGym's, and our mapping capped the drive.

Our 1 Oct fair test on the sugar reflex: real wiring 85.2 ± 3.56 Hz; degree-preserving and weight shuffles 0 Hz; boundary-preserving 39 Hz (retention 0.46); sign shuffle 214 Hz with the whole brain ignited. The gain-matched arm was not matched on 3 shuffles; the row stays mixed, unfair and weak.

Where the wiring helps, a brain-free baseline often matches the fly anyway: the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 3 of 19 studies. In Doom (doom-fly-control by gabrycina) the fly survives 53.34 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s and a brainless autopilot 51.93 s.

Build your own: tested 28 Sep 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs (MN9 85.2 Hz real, 0 Hz shuffled) and re-tested 5 Oct 2026 (6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz bit-exact). Tested deeper steps: Add a body (2 Oct, FlyGym 2.1.0, our mapping) and Add a sense: looming (5 Oct, exact commands and source published).

Does it actually run? (our browser check of 3 Oct 2026, headless Chromium 154, Linux, no GPU; not a play test): Fly Worker 17.55 MB, FLY67 33.28 MB and flybrain.app 12.72 MB ran; FlyLeno and Help the Fly Escape froze after loading; fly-brain (Lulzx) stopped at our 1.6 GB memory limit. No demo computed on a server. flybrain.app's page says a language model ('Claude') acts as the fly's caretaker, on the fly's world, not inside its brain model.

New entries (5 Oct 2026): Flight-test the fly (A), FlyAim (A, a pre-registered negative result), FlyArm (B) and FlyWireGBA (C, a Game Boy Advance fly whose 128-neuron FlyWire subgraph only gates feeding).

"I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (868,853 views on 5 Oct 2026) and a Roblox fight video: both grade U, no code. A driving compilation (107,515 views) appears to show Flyhard (B), matched from its thumbnail only. The two most-viewed Minecraft fly videos (French, 575,059; Spanish, 475,569) map to no catalogued project.
Video gallery (5 Oct 2026): 53 videos, each with a language field (51 English, 2 Russian); a Russian explainer by DenTrave added; all available. Thumbnails unchanged.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 in FlyWire's guidelines (non-commercial; the Zenodo v783 record says CC BY 4.0, and we follow the stricter reading); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.
uncertainty: Our looming test (5 Oct 2026): One model (Shiu et al. LIF on FlyWire v783), open loop, our hand-made mapping, a constant external walking drive, 1 s; not a real fly. Small n: 4 real runs and 3 scrambled runs, not 6 and 6, because a looming trial took about 160 s and the pre-registered clock cuts fired; the 3 scrambled runs sent drives identical to the no-brain floor, so in effect they are one walk; the '5 of 6' rule was applied as a share (4 of 4), decided before any body run. The scrambled brains were much quieter (activity ratio 0.50) and no activity-matched scramble was reached, so the ledger rates the comparison unfair and weak. The 'away' direction rests on our mapping's DNa02 sign and fly67's claim: fly67's claim; the direction in real flies was not verified by us. The stimulus is strong and artificial (every LC4 and LPLC2 of one eye at 80 Hz); the giant-fibre-off and gain-matched arms were not run.

The four plain answers rest on our reading of project files (the trained-part classes), one primary nociception source and our licence reading, which is not legal advice; whether CC BY or CC BY-NC applies to a FlyWire release is an open question with FlyWire.

Our body test covers one stimulus (P9 at 150 Hz on both sides), one brain model, one body, 1 s of open-loop walking, 3 trial seeds and 3 shuffles that sent identical drives. The rate-to-drive mapping is ours: it caps the drive at 1.2, so another mapping could let the wiring matter more. The pre-registered P9 sign, other P9 rates and other descending neuron types were not tested in the body.

Our fair test covers one reflex (sugar to MN9) in one model, with one 1 s trial per shuffle at one trial seed; the MN9 rate cannot tell selective drive from global ignition. The gain-matched arm is not matched on 3 shuffles; a per-shuffle gain search has not been run.

Browser check: one headless Chromium 154 on Linux without a GPU, 60-90 s per demo, one action each; not a play test. Both freezes most likely come from software WebGL on our machine; GPU machines, Safari, Firefox and phones were not tested. Activity detection is coarse (screenshots every 5 s), bytes cover only the first 60-90 s, and traffic in cross-origin frames is not counted. Protocol completions and three deviations (a tool bug fixed and re-run within the 2-load limit) were written down but not pre-registered by the planner. View counts come from YouTube search pages; the Terraria, Gorilla Tag and Roblox fight videos were not watched.
The Terraria verdict rests on code older than the video; fly-walking-wiring's B is provisional because its results are not public. The Flyhard match of the driving compilation rests on one thumbnail.

Controls ledger: every number except our own three tests is the authors'. We recomputed 17 studies from their committed files but re-ran none; none is replicated, and only 2 of 38 are peer-reviewed. Only 12 of 38 studies reach "strong" method quality; 20 are weak. fly-cartpole's new numbers were not recomputed and its real arm sits at the 500-step ceiling; ChessFly rests on one fly and one shuffle per arm.

Ledger labels (wiring effect, fairness, quality) come from fixed yes/no rules applied to code and files; they are consistent but coarse. Our body test scores strong although its 3 shuffles behaved as one; our reflex test is "mixed" by rule although its arms read silent, partly and runaway. We did not override the rules for our own rows. Activity fields are reported only for our two tests. Retention puts very different measurements on one scale. The flyvis ablation values exist only in a figure and were not extracted; our text search of its supplement was crude (no PDF tool).

The "helps" results are mostly one kind of test (does a reflex pathway still carry signal after rewiring?), which is a low bar; boundary-preserving nulls have been applied to one reflex (ours: 46% kept), not to the other reflex studies.

Borderline grades: FlyLeno (B, borderline C); Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving, the null-model study and fly-brain-zero-shot are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B; acamilo-flybrain would sit on the B/C border without its stream macros.

Several C grades and the fafbseg entry rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line. fly-plays-games runs its neurons in an external package (fly.ai) that we did not inspect beyond its commit subjects.

The Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim are known only through news articles, a Reddit post and a Twitch page read through summarising tools or search summaries; X, TikTok and Reddit cannot be searched without a login.
Stars, creation and last-push dates of some records were reused from earlier checks and are labelled with those dates in projects.json.

Not yet triaged: about 30 new low-star repositories from this week, leads deferred in earlier weeks, about 211 repositories listed only in directories, and 42 small repositories from this week and an LC4/LPLC2 escape study whose results are not committed yet.

Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated. The attractor reported for the Shiu et al. model has not been reproduced by us.

The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. Add a body is tested on Linux CPU only, without rendering. DOOMFLY's and DesktopFly's run steps are untested by us.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.
Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots.

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.
